notes: Denver and some other Colorado cities set higher local minimum wages; no city files yet.
Drafted from US DOL WHD state tables (confidence=medium) on 2026-11-06; upgrade to primary sources pending.
minimum_wage.effective is the DOL table date (2026-11-05), not the statutory effective date.

Minors (CDLE INFO #22A summarizing C.R.S. § 8-12-105; statute text is LexisNexis-hosted): all minors under 18 are capped at 8 h/24 h and 40 h/week (seasonal piece-rate harvest exceptions). Under-16 state-only limits: 6 h on a school day, no work 9:30 p.m.-5 a.m. before school days (CO.minor_limits.1 enforces 9:30 p.m. every night of a school week, stricter). 7 CCR 1103-20 (youth rules) has no hour limits.
Minimum wage: CDLE INFO #22A confirms $15.16 for 2026; effective date left at the date first seen (the source gives no start date).

Tipped minimum wage: cash wage = $15.16 − $3.02 tip credit (CDLE INFO #22A states the $3.02 credit; the adult tip rules are in INFO #3, not fetched). Denver and other cities set higher local wages (no city files).

rules.summary: Colorado's 2026 minimum wage is $15.16 an hour (CDLE).

citation.title: CDLE INFO #22A — Employment of Minors, Minimum Wages, Hours (C.R.S. § 8-12-105), June 3, 2026
citation.excerpt: Employers can pay most minors 85% of the full Colorado minimum wage — for example, in 2026, $12.89 rather than the full $15.16 minimum.

rules.summary: Under Colorado law, minors under 16 may work at most 6 hours on a school day (unless the next day is not a school day), 8 hours in 24 and 40 a week, not 9:30 p.m.-5 a.m. before school days; federal 3 h / 18 h / 7 p.m. limits also apply where FLSA covers the employer.

citation.excerpt: If state but not federal law applies, the CYEOA limit is: at most 6 hours per day, unless the next day isn't a school day. C.R.S. § 8-12-105(2).
